problem: Determinantal conjecture on the determinant of the sum of two normal matrices
missing_details: Specification that A and B are n×n matrices over the complex field
Definition of “normal” (A A* = A* A) to ensure diagonalizability
Introduction of eigenvalues λ_i(A) and λ_i(B) and their labeling
Definition of the symmetric group S_n and its elements σ
Construction of the n! complex numbers z_σ = ∏_{i=1}^n (λ_i(A) + λ_{σ(i)}(B))
Precise condition that det(A+B) lies in the convex hull of {z_σ: σ ∈ S_n}
refined_question: Let A and B be n×n normal matrices over the complex numbers, and let λ_1(A),…,λ_n(A) and λ_1(B),…,λ_n(B) denote their eigenvalues. For each permutation σ in the symmetric group S_n, define the complex number z_σ=∏_{i=1}^n(λ_i(A)+λ_{σ(i)}(B)). Is it true that det(A+B) lies in the convex hull of the set {z_σ: σ∈S_n} in the complex plane?
justification: The original problem name indicates only that it concerns the determinant of a sum of two normal matrices, but omits key ingredients such as the eigenvalue-based construction of n! candidate points, the convex hull condition, and the role of the symmetric group indexing permutations. The refined question incorporates all required notation and definitions verbatim from the canonical source without broadening or weakening the conjecture.
